SYDNEY, 2 February 2017 — Jamaica Blue believes in giving back to the community and that begins with the nation’s youth\. The company has committed to a long-term partnership with Beacon Foundation – the national charity organisation supporting young people from disadvantaged communities to complete Year 12 and successfully transition into meaningful careers\.

Drew Eide, Brand Manager at Jamaica Blue, believes the partnership is a perfect fit, in that both organisations value working with young Australians to ensure they have the skills, capabilities and opportunities to be successful in life and work\.

“We employ over 1,500 people in our cafés across Australia and a large number of those are under the age of 25\. We are proud of Jamaica Blue’s record of creating employment opportunities for young people and giving them an introduction to the world of work, and we see Beacon Foundation’s Programs as an extension of that,” said Drew\.

To kick off the partnership, Jamaica Blue hosted a showcase program at their headquarters in Sydney\. 15 high school students from Nepean CAPA took part in a one-day workshop as part of the Polish Program to develop a range of relevant job-seeking skills\.

“The students were really impressive, embracing the concept of creating brand personas as well as understanding the kind of skills employers look for and how to sell themselves in the context of a job interview,” said Drew\. “It was a rewarding day and we’re looking forward to working closely with the Beacon Foundation and our local Jamaica Blue communities to encourage more young students to establish meaningful careers\.”

Scott Harris, CEO of Beacon Foundation says they are incredibly excited to work with Jamaica Blue to inspire young people across the country\. “The great thing about this partnership is giving franchisees the opportunity to make a difference to the lives of young people in their local communities\. We’re hoping to be able to assist many more students, in areas that need it most, to be better prepared to transition successfully into the workforce,” he says\.

For more information, visit Jamaica Blue at www\.jamaicablue\.com\.au and the Beacon Foundation at www\.beaconfoundation\.com\.au  
Michelle Bartolo

Justin Dale Goldsberry, 34, of Duncan, Oklahoma, passed away on May 13, 2026, in Duncan\.

Justin was born on August 7, 1991, in Duncan, Oklahoma, to Shannon Dale Jones and Caroline Goldsberry\. He spent his life in Duncan and was known for his kind and caring heart, his love of sports, and his deep love for family and friends\.

Justin accepted Christ and was baptized at City Heights Baptist Church in Duncan in 2001\. He attended Empire High School and graduated with the Class of 2010\. During high school, he especially loved sports and proudly played football, basketball, and baseball, earning his letters and proudly wearing his letterman’s jacket\. Baseball was always his favorite sport, and he loved the Texas Rangers as well as the Dallas Cowboys football team\.

Those who knew Justin will remember his love for his family, his caring nature, and the joy he brought to the people around him\.

Justin is survived by his parents, Shannon Dale Jones and Caroline Goldsberry; his grandparents, Robert and Shernell Jones; his two sons, Jackson and Timothy; and many other family members and friends who loved him dearly\.

Funeral services will be held Saturday, May 23, 2026, at 2:00 p\.m\. at Carter-Smart Funeral Home Chapel in Duncan, Oklahoma\. Burial will follow at Duncan Cemetery\.

Pallbearers will be Robert Jones Jr\., Gary Skidmore, Samuel Henderson, Jacob Henderson, Lynn Snow, and Joe Price\.

In lieu of flowers, donations may be made to the Beacon Foundation in Duncan, Oklahoma\. https://beaconfoundations\.org

The family would like to thank everyone for their prayers, love, and support during this difficult time\. The service will be a celebration of Justin’s life and the memories shared with those who loved him\.

# Busing company settles $2\.4 million lawsuit for colluding to raise prices in three Massachusetts communities, AG says - The Boston Globe

An Ohio-based school bus company has agreed to pay $2\.4 million to settle a lawsuit alleging it colluded with a competitor to inflate prices in three communities, Lynn, Dedham, and Saugus, between 2022 and 2025, Attorney General Andrea Campbell said Monday\.

Beacon Mobility Corporation, which mainly provides special education busing service through** **a pair of subsidiaries, agreed to settle accusations that it worked with an unnamed competitor to fix busing rates and undermine the competitive bidding process, Campbell said\.

According to the settlement, Beacon inflated contract prices by agreeing not to compete with the other company over certain district contracts in exchange for it doing the same in communities where Beacon held the contract\.

“When companies engage in unlawful collusion that increase costs for municipalities, it reduces their ability to fund other critical programs including our libraries, public safety agencies and schools,” Campbell said in a statement\.

A spokesperson for Campbell’s office, which pursued legal action against Beacon,** **declined to disclose the name of the other company, citing an ongoing investigation\.

It is unclear exactly how much the price fixing cost the three communities but Campbell said they will receive the majority of the $2\.4 million\.

Beacon also agreed to maintain an internal antitrust compliance program for at least five years, cooperate in future investigations, and report any efforts by competitors to rig bids or pass along sensitive bidding information, Campbell said\.

Beacon will also be required to notify Campbell’s office if it acquires any other transportation companies in the next 10 years, according to the settlement\.

“We are pleased this matter is resolved so we can remain focused on providing reliable and safe transportation services for the communities we serve,” Scott Sheridan, senior vice president for Beacon Mobility’s New England operations, said in a statement\.

The company said it provides busing for 500 districts across the country\.

According to the lawsuit, in May 2022 Beacon considered bidding for a three-year busing contract in Saugus, where its unnamed competitor had held the contract\.

But the company ultimately declined to bid, the settlement stated\. In internal emails, a Beacon employee wrote that they wouldn’t want to “take … work,” from the company, which was “very good not taking stuff from us\.”

“I know \[they\] won’t come to Lynn next year,” the employee wrote in the exchange, according to the settlement, also noting the company didn’t have the capacity to take on the contract\.

As predicted, Beacon’s subsidiary was the only bidder that summer for Lynn’s contract, the settlement said\.

Also in May and June of 2022, the unnamed company proposed extending its contract with Dedham while raising its price significantly, according to the settlement\.

While that proposal was being worked out, a Beacon employee spoke with a member of the other company by phone, relaying in a later internal email that** **the competitor’s employee “was hoping we do not underbid her stuff and she won’t to us\.”

Simultaneously, Beacon was approached by Dedham officials about taking over in-district transportation for special education students instead of the other company, which had just proposed a large rate hike\.

Beacon did not follow up and the other company retained the contract, the settlement stated\.

“Like us, they need to get their rates up as well and now all the business managers are freaking out,” the Beacon employee wrote in an email, according to the settlement\.

“This vendor’s corrupt exploitation of our district’s efforts to get some of our most vulnerable students to school is shameful,” Lynn Mayor Jared Nicholsonsaid in a statement on Monday\. “We very much appreciate the Attorney General and her team for holding them accountable and returning their ill-gotten gains back to our taxpayers\.”

# Beacon: Q2 Earnings Snapshot - WTOP News

BOSTON \(AP\) — BOSTON \(AP\) — Beacon Financial Corporation \(BBT\) on Wednesday reported second-quarter net income of $64\.4 million\.
